s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic skin condition characterized by vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules with a 2-week history, involving the face, scalp, trunk, and extremities, with a painful and itchy course
salient_findings: Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk
Difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils on histopathology
key_facts: 2-week history of skin lesions
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Prior treatment included prednisolone, clindamycin, and fluconazole
Patient continued to develop new lesions despite treatment
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk
Keloidal plaques were seen on the face
Patient reported difficulty walking due to skin lesions
HIV test was negative
Histopathology showed epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration was seen on histopathology
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils were seen on histopathology

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by painful, itchy plaques and pustules, matching the patient's symptoms and histopathology findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, and histopathology findings of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses

shortlist.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by widespread pustules and plaques, matching the patient's symptoms, and histopathology findings of epidermal hyperplasia and microabscesses

shortlist.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by subcorneal pustules and matching the patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's symptoms of widespread pustules and plaques, and histopathology findings of dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques that began as pustules and developed into vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses scattered with eosinophils, is most consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum. The patient's lack of response to prior treatments and the presence of systemic symptoms such as difficulty walking due to skin lesions also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sweet syndrome
rejected.why: While Sweet syndrome can present with similar skin lesions, the patient's histopathology did not show the characteristic granulocytes and the patient did not have a clear infectious or inflammatory trigger.

rejected.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions did not have the characteristic appearance of psoriatic plaques and the histopathology did not show the typical findings of psoriasis, such as parakeratosis and Munro's microabscesses.

rejected.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions were not limited to the subcorneal region and the histopathology did not show the characteristic subcorneal pustules.

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation was not typical of an acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, which is usually triggered by a medication or infection and presents with a more widespread and symmetric distribution of pustules.
